messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Stan Beta release
parts:
I'm thinking we should start with an official
beta release at the end of February. That's to let
people know things may be a bit rough for the
first few users until we see how things go.

Other than doc (which is what I'm focusing on
now), the only remaining necessary code to-do
items are:

-- discrete slice sampler for unbounded
integer parameters

-- diagonal mass matrix estimation

I'm more concerned about the latter than the
former given our trouble with scaling in Ben's
logistic regression example.

There are also a whole bunch of nice-to-have
items relating to efficiency and a few related
to easier debugging.

Also, should I be recording the total log
probability function value in each saved iteration
along with the samples? It's not a parameter and
we don't really want to test its convergence,
but it might be nice to include.

And of course, there's an actual R interface
instead of the file-based round-trips we have now.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: added log prob to parameter output
parts:
> Also, should I be recording the total log
> probability function value in each saved iteration
> along with the samples? It's not a parameter and
> we don't really want to test its convergence,
> but it might be nice to include.

I just went ahead and added it as the first column
with header "lp__". That matches the name used in
the code and thus avoids conflicts with Stan parameters.
And it's parsable by R's CSV reader.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan Beta release
parts:
1. I thought we were delaying the unbounded integer parameters for now, since there are none of these in the Bugs example.

2. The diagonal mass matrix estimation is part of Nuts2, I believe.

3. We can also talk (tomorrow at 1) about post-processing: R-hat, effective sample size, graphical summary, Waic, etc. We'll do all or most of these in R, I assume?
